messages.content: how to get the information of an interface?

function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
To retrieve telemetry data for a specific interface you’ll need to call the **`telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`** function and supply the following five pieces of information:

| Parameter | What it represents | Example value |
|-----------|--------------------|---------------|
| `fabricName` | Name of the fabric that contains the node | `"fabricA"` |
| `nodeId` | Identifier of the node (usually a numeric ID) | `101` |
| `podId` | Identifier of the pod that contains the node | `5` |
| `interfaceType` | Type of interface you’re interested in (`"svi"`, `"ethernet"`, `"loopback"`, `"port‑channel"`) | `"ethernet"` |
| `infoType` | Kind of data you want (`"interfaces"`, `"status"`, `"statistics"`, `"errors"`) | `"statistics"` |

### Example call

```python
result = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get({
    "fabricName": "fabricA",
    "nodeId": 101,
    "podId": 5,
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",
    "infoType": "statistics"
})
print(result)
```

This will return the requested telemetry data for all Ethernet interfaces on node 101 in pod 5 of fabric “A”, specifically the statistics for each interface.

If you only want a single interface (e.g., `Ethernet1/1`), you can filter the returned list in your code or, if the API supports it, pass an additional filter parameter (not shown here).
